content:
Oratomic CEO Dolev Bluvstein will discuss neutral-atom quantum processors at the Pasadena campus talk

Richard P. Feynman Lecture Hall [photo credit: CALTECH]

Caltech has scheduled a Physics Colloquium on its Pasadena campus from 4 p.m. to 5 p.m. on Thursday, Oct. 1, at East Bridge 201, the Richard P. Feynman Lecture Hall, according to Caltech’s online events calendar. The talk is part of the Physics Colloquium Series and is sponsored by Caltech’s Division of Physics, Mathematics and Astronomy, the calendar listing states. A Zoom option is also listed for those who cannot attend in person.

Dolev Bluvstein, listed by Caltech as CEO of Oratomic and a visiting associate in physics at Caltech, is scheduled to speak on “Error-corrected quantum processing with neutral atoms.” According to the event description, quantum computers can open new scientific and computational possibilities only if they can be made fault-tolerant. The description says the complexity of controlling these machines and the large overhead required for error correction have made building one a longstanding challenge.

Bluvstein will describe quantum computing with reconfigurable arrays of neutral atoms and their use toward a fault-tolerant quantum computer, according to Caltech. In this approach, atoms are moved by optical tweezers. The listing says this allows any atom to connect with any other, high-fidelity programmable logic, and processing in the middle of a computation within a zoned architecture. The description adds that parallel control and long-range connectivity support experiments ranging from simulating quantum scrambling to building a universal fault-tolerant processing architecture.

The talk will also cover theoretical work that uses the processor’s long-range connectivity to reduce error-correction overhead, according to the listing. That work points to the potential for utility-scale computation with as few as 10,000 reconfigurable atomic qubits, the description states. Bluvstein is expected to discuss how the approach could enable fault-tolerant quantum computing in the near term.

Thursday, Oct. 1, 4 p.m. to 5 p.m. Richard P. Feynman Lecture Hall, East Bridge 201, Caltech, 1200 E. California Blvd., Pasadena. For more visit https://www.caltech.edu/campus-life-events/calendar/physics-colloquium-130. Join via Zoom at https://caltech.zoom.us/j/84497014003, meeting ID 844 9701 4003.
